openPoints: What bounds the memory and response-size impact of graph://claims?scope=snapshot when a tenant grows from thousands to millions of claims, given that the endpoint currently materializes every row and the browser replaces its complete claims cache in one operation?

How does QueryBar leave loading state when a request is already in flight and the user clears the input, since clearing advances the sequence and returns before setting loading false while the superseded request is no longer allowed to clear it?

What prevents an older snapshot claims request from overwriting a newer forced refresh when readSnapshotClaims(true) replaces the shared promise but does not sequence or abort the underlying requests?

How should navigation behave when loadSnapshot or the forced claims projection fails after a dangling-reference click, given that the async RefChip handler has no local error boundary and recovery feedback depends on the earlier generic toast?
architectureTip: Keep the snapshot projection as the consistency boundary, then add pagination or versioned responses and apply the same latest-request discipline used by QueryBar to all cache-refresh paths.
